## Result

- Skill: code-review.
- Status: completed.
- Review status: approved.
- Assessment scope: final whole-change.
- Review record: code-review-final.json.
- Exact final basis:56d8000d..775a50b9; engineering final f51445a4 plus attributable evidence/Route tail.
- Reviewed milestone: none; complete delivered initiative and cross-milestone interactions.
- Milestone closeout: not-applicable to this final assessment; primary context reports m1 and m2 completed.
- Remaining implementation milestones: none.
- Material findings / open blockers / required review-resolution: none found within this assessment.
- Recording status: targeted v2 review.record; reviewer changes only own final review.
- Next stage: Route hands off to distinct final Verify.
- Verify readiness: not-claimed as a Verify result; the required independent whole-change Code Review checkpoint is satisfied for these exact subjects.
- No branch-ready, PR-ready, CI-success, release, publication, customer adoption or final completion claim.

## Fresh whole-change assessment

I reset scope from milestone implementation to the entire delivered change: proposal direction, Design/System/Workflow/retained installer amendment, stable plan and proof allocation, original M1 transaction plus all corrections, M2 public method/resource/consumer/installer/validator/metadata changes, source retirement and follow-up ownership. I inspected the complete change manifest and actual relevant hunks, reread governing requirements and the transaction/public-caller composition, and checked current context and evidence. Earlier stage approvals establish their own exact authority, not this final conclusion.

The delivered capability addresses the approved challenge rather than merely renaming authors. One model owner now holds observable behavior, realization, decision rationale, boundaries and acceptance intent. The System view identifies its composition obligation and shared owners; Workflow references the transferred convention instead of retaining a competing definition. The installed common procedure and conditional resources support both new model work and substantively amended retained feature/architecture/ADR contracts. Independent Design Review consumes exact owners, relevant consumers, legacy members and examples, including new example identity when the parent is unchanged. Delivery still allocates commands/fixtures/integrated proof; implementation supplies results; Review and Closeout/Test/Verify retain their separate duties.

The actual transition is coherent across authored source, source validator inventory, shared resource projections and identities, adapter manifests/aliases, current measured candidate metadata, public installer guards and operator documentation. Both retired skill directories and aliases are removed from the committed/public candidate set, not left as parallel redirect contracts. Complete installed methods have no internal checkout dependency. Customer authority remains supplied by the customer; installation does not activate this repository's policy there. Current source notices are explicitly bounded to selected responsibilities, preserve historical evidence and unselected owners, and condition adopted reliance on reviewed implementation and successful Verify.

## Cross-milestone interactions and proof

| Composed boundary | Independent whole-change judgment and direct basis |
| --- | --- |
| Approved direction to one engineering method | Proposal constraints remain respected: bounded first consolidation, no complete-repository migration, no new workflow gate/schema/service, no guaranteed token reduction. DES/SYS requirements and scoped TNI amendment supply the selected behavioral authority. |
| M1 private transaction to M2 public dispatch | Original hash/root/state eligibility is captured before asynchronous archive work; the synchronous helper rechecks it before mutation. Candidate trust and retired inventory checks precede replacement. Installed roots are verified before shared state publication. Public tests exercise real dispatch, so helper-only evidence does not stand in for integration. |
| Publication to failure/retry | Pinned-parent basename operations and no-clobber publication preserve independent bytes; root/ancestor checks and late-write backups remain. Private recovery evidence blocks mixed/drifted pairs; caught failures restore the unchanged original or report conflict/partial recovery. Real process interruption then documented operator restoration and successful retry are shown against the same archive. |
| Multiple target roots and shared state | OpenCode skills/commands are selected together. Other managed targets and unrelated files/state entries survive. State-implicated ownership cannot take the unmanaged cleanup path; genuinely unmanaged cleanup remains explicitly inspected/backed-up scoped removal followed by ordinary conflict checks. |
| Model/scenario authoring to independent assessment and proof allocation | MW-01 produced concrete three-target customer artifacts and exact handoffs for shared-contract coordination, retained feature amendment, architecture/ADR aid, product conflict, missing guidance versus missing project authority, parseable invariant-breaking pair and separate example-only applicability. Those observations support semantic sufficiency beyond package-presence tests. |
| Authority migration to validators/current navigation | MW-02 traces all material numbered/unnumbered obligations and selected system sections; old decisions and method bodies are retained with replacement ownership. The narrow validator checks immutable two-source preservation and contained replacement owners rather than requiring an obsolete source to become a new feature contract. It cannot infer semantic approval from an archive heading or unknown marker. |
| Canonical resources to supported packages | Same exact candidate hashes bind method walkthrough, archive validation/clean installs, current metadata and actual operator run. Codex/Claude/OpenCode resources and aliases reflect one author; conditional resource dependencies and generic aids close within the package. |
| Milestone completion to final closeout | Both implementation entries are completed, all original finding dispositions are resolved, and the plan's independent final review then distinct Verify sequence remains explicit. No author/evidence save, generated-package pass or milestone approval substitutes for this review or successful Verify. |

## First-pass checklist

1. Spec alignment: pass. The complete delivered behavior conforms to current Design r6/Delivery r3 and approved proposal constraints; engineering additions remain the named first slice.
2. Test coverage: pass for final Code Review scope. Meaningful normal/negative/public/recovery/compatibility proof and manual semantic assessment cover the changed outcomes; representative scenarios are not treated as a whitelist.
3. Edge cases: pass. Modified/extra/missing/symlink/mixed roots, invalid candidate/aliases, ordinary/dry-run, all target roots, restored/idempotent retry, failed rollback and concurrent shared-state protection have direct evidence.
4. Error handling: pass. Preflight failures do not publish; incomplete recovery stays explicit and preserves retained bytes rather than resetting state. Missing package guidance versus missing project authority has distinct owned correction.
5. Architecture boundaries: pass. Shared policy, component contracts, system composition, semantic coordination and CLI mechanics retain one owner each.
6. Compatibility: pass. Original artifact/protocol/placement and historical release identities are not renamed into public skill invocations; legacy sources keep their format/IDs unless mapped for this bounded transfer.
7. Security/privacy: pass. No new external service/credential or arbitrary migration authority; archive trust, state/root basis, no-clobber operations, operator permissions and unrelated-content preservation remain.
8. Derived currency: pass for the exact local candidate only. Source/archive/installed inventory and measured metadata match; no release report/notes or publication outcome is fabricated.
9. Unrelated changes: pass. Directly required consumer/selector/projection/test changes and narrow retirement enforcement stay within the approved responsibility. Remaining consolidation has FU-012–014 owners/next actions, not hidden present-scope deferral. User docs/design.zip is preserved.
10. Validation evidence: pass within stated limits. Actual full-suite and targeted/manual results support the delivered behavior; failed baseline evidence retains its meaning and distinct Verify applicability remains necessary.

## Current evidence, prior findings and limits

Current author evidence reports454 Node,355 skill-validator,156 selector,87 boundary,158 adapter-distribution,7 skill-build and7 npm-publication tests passing, plus projection, model/lifecycle, prose/readability, package and three-target clean-install checks. In the immediately preceding independent M2 review I executed38 helper,16 public DES and3 retired-source tests successfully. No engineering bytes changed afterward, so I retain those exact results without representing them as a newly executed full suite or rerunning unchanged checks merely to create freshness. This fresh judgment is based on independent whole-change analysis as well as that evidence.

MW-01 and MW-02 inspected source subjects remain current. The MW-03 exercised CLI/helper/guide/metadata and candidate remain unchanged; its stored test-file subject precedes three added complementary tests. As explicitly assessed in M2, that added-only test change does not alter the actual walkthrough execution; the old execution subject stays preserved and current tests supply separate proof. MW-03 transcript contains ordinary rejection, authorized success, exit97 interruption, partial retry rejection, operator restoration, success and idempotent retry with actual archives and an unchanged old managed neighbor. No uncontrolled power-loss or target-agent correctness claim follows.

All original design findings des-review-f1–f5 and implementation m1-review-f1/f2 are resolved by their reporter with original origins/history preserved. I inspected the resolved concerns against the final remedies: full example/mapping obligations, executable managed upgrade, complete packaged legacy guidance, one mapping owner, correct every-cited-boundary example ownership, no-clobber publication and both-endpoint/root authority. Their prior approval labels alone did not establish final correctness.

Historical method body/notice hashes and both original ADR bytes are preserved. Older proposal references to retired source paths identify the inspected drafting basis; current Design displacement mappings and base Git identities provide explicit replacement/history access rather than rewriting old approval evidence. The current retained installer amendment's drafting caveats do not supply implementation authority or contradict its normative outcomes; actual execution evidence remains in the change record.

The two old architecture-method new-feature-marker failures remain recorded historical failed observations. Current selected validation uses the specifically reviewed preservation path and passes. The13 unchanged historical installer prose errors remain failed baseline evidence, with exact unchanged-body comparison and the plan's scoped limitation; I do not relabel them passing or grant a blanket exemption to touched documents. Verify must independently assess applicability and completion. All package claims here are local-candidate claims; separate release/publication/customer adoption authority is unchanged.

## Independence

Concrete independent nonauthor /root/independent_design_review. Primary-agent authored proposal/model/plan/implementation contributions under user direction; reviewer authored none of those production subjects. This fresh whole-change pass evaluated the complete delivered diff and end-to-end interactions, rather than combining milestone approval labels into final authority. Reviewer-owned synthetic customer fixtures and prior reviews provide inspectable supporting evidence only.
